# File reference

Every file in the project: what it is, how it is done, what it uses and where it is used.

*Generated by `npm run docs` (`pipeline/gen-docs.mjs`). The descriptions are written in `pipeline/doc-notes.mjs`; the "Uses", "Used by", "Exports" and line counts are read from the code. Do not edit this file by hand: `pipeline/docs.test.mjs` fails when it is out of date.*

**Where code runs:** *Browser* = in the visitor's browser; *Node (build)* = on a developer's computer or in GitHub Actions while building and testing; *Browser + Node* = the same file is used by both; *Not code* = text, data, images.

## Contents

- Project root (6 files)
- docs/: documentation (7 files)
- core/: code shared by the build and the app (9 files)
- core/art/: the crochet pictures (6 files)
- pipeline/: build tools and tests (Node only) (19 files)
- server/: local web server (1 file)
- web/: the app that runs in the browser (21 files)

69 files in total.

## Project root

### `.github/workflows/pages.yml`

**What it is.** Builds the whole site from source and publishes it to GitHub Pages every time something is pushed to `main`.

**How it is done.** Two jobs. `build`: check out, Node 24 (with npm cache), `npm ci`, `npm run fetch` (download Bible texts), `npm run build` (data + art), `npm test`, `npm run export`, then upload `dist/web` as the Pages artifact. `deploy`: publishes the artifact. A failing test stops the run, so a broken change is never published. Can also be started by hand ("Run workflow").

**Runs in:** GitHub Actions · 46 lines

**Uses:** npm scripts in package.json · eBible.org (downloads during the build) · GitHub Pages (source must be set to "GitHub Actions" in the repository settings)

**Used by:** GitHub runs it automatically on every push to `main`

### `.gitignore`

**What it is.** Keeps generated and downloaded things out of the repository.

**How it is done.** Ignores `node_modules/`, `data/raw/` (downloaded Bible texts, about 300 MB), `dist/` (built data and the exported site), `.DS_Store` and `.claude/` (local preview settings). All ignored folders are recreated by `npm ci`, `npm run fetch`, `npm run build` and `npm run export`.

**Runs in:** Not code · 6 lines

**Used by:** git

### `ATTRIBUTION.md`

**What it is.** The licenses and required credits for all 11 Bible texts, plus credits for SQLite and the artwork.

**How it is done.** Generated by `pipeline/gen-attribution.mjs` from the registry in `pipeline/versions.mjs`, so the credits cannot differ from what the app shows. Do not edit by hand.

**Runs in:** Not code · 84 lines

**Used by:** People reading the repository; the same text is shown inside the app (Settings, Credits and licenses)

### `README.md`

**What it is.** The front page: what the app is, how to run it, how it is hosted, how search and pictures work, the live address and the known limits.

**How it is done.** Written by hand. The detailed documentation lives in the `docs/` folder.

**Runs in:** Not code · 103 lines

**Used by:** People reading the repository on GitHub

### `package-lock.json`

**What it is.** The exact version of every installed package.

**How it is done.** Written by npm. `npm ci` in the workflow installs exactly these versions so builds are repeatable.

**Runs in:** Not code · 30 lines

**Used by:** npm ci

### `package.json`

**What it is.** Project definition: the one dependency, the Node version, and the npm scripts for every task.

**How it is done.** Scripts: `fetch`, `build`, `build:art`, `search`, `export`, `icons`, `docs`, `serve`, `test`. Only one dependency, `@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm` (SQLite compiled to WebAssembly). `"type": "module"` makes every `.mjs`/`.js` file an ES module. Requires Node 24 or newer because the build uses the built-in `node:sqlite`.

**Runs in:** Not code · 24 lines

**Uses:** npm registry

**Used by:** npm · GitHub Actions workflow

## core/: code shared by the build and the app

### `core/archaic.gen.mjs`

**What it is.** A generated map of 1,146 old-English verb forms to modern ones ("believeth" to "believe", "hath" to "have").

**How it is done.** Written by `pipeline/gen-archaic.mjs`. A word is only mapped if it never appears in the modern texts (WEB and BSB) but its base word does, so real words such as "earnest", "forest" and "faith" stay untouched. Three wrong results found by reading the list ("badest", "marieth", "thoughtest") are blocked by name.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 2 lines

**Uses:** generated from the downloaded English texts in data/raw

**Used by:** [`core/english.mjs`](../core/english.mjs)

**Exports:** `ARCHAIC_FORMS`

### `core/bible.mjs`

**What it is.** The `Bible` class: the one API for books, chapters, verse texts, reference lookup and keyword search.

**How it is done.** Works on a core database plus one "shard" database per version, through a tiny interface `db.all(sql, params)`. Node wraps `node:sqlite`; the browser wraps SQLite WebAssembly, so exactly the same code runs in both. A search plans the query (`core/query.mjs`), runs it on the full-text index of every loaded shard (capped at 4,000 hits per shard), merges hits per verse across versions keeping the best BM25 score, then pages the result. An optional `range` limits a search to a testament or one book using a rowid range.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 168 lines

**Uses:** [`core/books.mjs`](../core/books.mjs) · [`core/reference.mjs`](../core/reference.mjs) · [`core/query.mjs`](../core/query.mjs) · core.db and the per-version shard databases (built by `pipeline/build-data.mjs`)

**Used by:** [`pipeline/cli.mjs`](../pipeline/cli.mjs) · [`pipeline/node-bible.mjs`](../pipeline/node-bible.mjs) · [`web/js/data.mjs`](../web/js/data.mjs)

**Exports:** `DEFAULT_VERSION`, `Bible`

### `core/books.mjs`

**What it is.** The 66 books of the Bible with English and Tamil names, about 390 name spellings, and the verse reference id format.

**How it is done.** A verse id is `book*1000000 + chapter*1000 + verse` (John 3:16 is 43003016). The alias table lists full names, codes and short forms in both languages; building it throws if two books share an alias, so ambiguities are found at once. Tamil names come from `tamil-names.gen.mjs`.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 127 lines

**Uses:** [`core/tamil-names.gen.mjs`](../core/tamil-names.gen.mjs)

**Used by:** [`core/bible.mjs`](../core/bible.mjs) · [`core/reference.mjs`](../core/reference.mjs) · [`pipeline/build-data.mjs`](../pipeline/build-data.mjs) · [`pipeline/text-utils.test.mjs`](../pipeline/text-utils.test.mjs) · [`pipeline/vpl.mjs`](../pipeline/vpl.mjs) · [`web/js/art-view.mjs`](../web/js/art-view.mjs) · [`web/js/ui.mjs`](../web/js/ui.mjs) · [`web/js/views.mjs`](../web/js/views.mjs)

**Exports:** `aliasKey`, `BOOKS`, `BOOK_BY_VPL`, `BOOK_BY_ID`, `ALIAS_INDEX`, `refId`, `splitRef`

### `core/english.mjs`

**What it is.** English text helpers for search: split into words, fold old-English forms, and prepare a verse for indexing.

**How it is done.** The same functions run on indexed verses (build) and on typed queries (browser), so "believeth" and "believe" meet at one index term. Porter stemming itself is done by SQLite's FTS5 tokenizer.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 13 lines

**Uses:** [`core/archaic.gen.mjs`](../core/archaic.gen.mjs)

**Used by:** [`core/art/spec.mjs`](../core/art/spec.mjs) · [`core/query.mjs`](../core/query.mjs) · [`pipeline/build-data.mjs`](../pipeline/build-data.mjs) · [`pipeline/text-utils.test.mjs`](../pipeline/text-utils.test.mjs)

**Exports:** `englishWords`, `foldArchaic`, `englishIndexForm`

### `core/query.mjs`

**What it is.** Turns what a person types into FTS5 queries: words, "exact phrases", -excluded words, prefix*, any-word (OR), and Tamil typed in English letters.

**How it is done.** `parseQuery` splits the input; `planQuery` decides which indexes to use (English, Tamil script, or the Tamil sound index) and builds the MATCH strings, always quoting terms so user input can never break the query syntax; `highlightRegex` builds the pattern used to mark matches on screen.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 99 lines

**Uses:** [`core/tamil.mjs`](../core/tamil.mjs) · [`core/english.mjs`](../core/english.mjs)

**Used by:** [`core/bible.mjs`](../core/bible.mjs) · [`pipeline/cli.mjs`](../pipeline/cli.mjs) · [`pipeline/text-utils.test.mjs`](../pipeline/text-utils.test.mjs) · [`web/js/views.mjs`](../web/js/views.mjs)

**Exports:** `parseQuery`, `planQuery`, `highlightRegex`

### `core/reference.mjs`

**What it is.** Reads typed references such as "John 3:16", "1 Cor 13", "II Kings 5.14", "யோவான் 3:16" into book, chapter and verse range, and writes references back out in either language.

**How it is done.** A regular expression splits name, chapter and verses; Roman numerals and "First/1st" are normalised; the name is looked up in the alias table. A bare book name is returned as a book (no chapter), so the UI can treat "Job" or "Mark" as ordinary search words.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 51 lines

**Uses:** [`core/books.mjs`](../core/books.mjs)

**Used by:** [`core/bible.mjs`](../core/bible.mjs) · [`pipeline/cli.mjs`](../pipeline/cli.mjs) · [`pipeline/text-utils.test.mjs`](../pipeline/text-utils.test.mjs) · [`web/js/ui.mjs`](../web/js/ui.mjs) · [`web/js/views.mjs`](../web/js/views.mjs)

**Exports:** `parseReference`, `formatReference`

### `core/scope.mjs`

**What it is.** Search scopes: the whole Bible, the Old or New Testament, or one book, as a range of verse ids.

**How it is done.** Returns `[lo, hi]` for `all`, `ot`, `nt` or `b<bookId>`, or null for everything. `core/bible.mjs` turns it into `rowid BETWEEN lo AND hi`.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 12 lines

**Used by:** [`pipeline/features.test.mjs`](../pipeline/features.test.mjs) · [`web/js/views.mjs`](../web/js/views.mjs)

**Exports:** `scopeRange`

### `core/tamil-names.gen.mjs`

**What it is.** The Tamil names of the 66 books.

**How it is done.** Extracted once from the headers (`\h`, `\toc1`, `\toc2`) of the Tamil IRV text in USFM format, so the names are the translation's own. They carry the same CC BY-SA 4.0 license as that text.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 334 lines

**Uses:** eBible.org tam2017_usfm.zip

**Used by:** [`core/books.mjs`](../core/books.mjs)

**Exports:** `TAMIL_NAMES`

### `core/tamil.mjs`

**What it is.** Everything Tamil-specific about search.

**How it is done.** SQLite's tokenizer treats Tamil vowel signs and the pulli as separators and would chop "அன்பு" into pieces, so those marks are mapped to private-use characters in the index only (the stored text is never changed). Queries drop the final vowel sign or pulli and match as a prefix, so one stem finds inflected forms (அன்பு, அன்பை, அன்பினால்). A second, lossy "sound" form turns Tamil script and English-letter typing ("anbu", "thevan", "devan") into the same key.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 157 lines

**Used by:** [`core/query.mjs`](../core/query.mjs) · [`pipeline/build-data.mjs`](../pipeline/build-data.mjs) · [`pipeline/text-utils.test.mjs`](../pipeline/text-utils.test.mjs)

**Exports:** `isTamilChar`, `hasTamil`, `tamilScriptForm`, `tamilTokens`, `stemToken`, `tamilWordToPhonetic`, `latinWordToPhonetic`, `tamilPhoneticForm`, `stemPhonetic`

## core/art/: the crochet pictures

### `core/art/compose.mjs`

**What it is.** Draws a verse's picture: a 48 by 32 stitch scene built from layers, with its own animation.

**How it is done.** Layers from back to front: sky (dithered bands), sun or moon, stars, shooting star, clouds, terrain for the setting (meadow, sea, mountain, desert, city, temple, garden, heaven, cave, field, river, house), the main figure and up to two more, weather (rain, lightning, embers, sparkles), flocks of birds. A random generator seeded by the verse reference (plus an optional "variant" number for the Shuffle button) places everything, so verses with the same subject still differ. `frame(t)` flattens the layers for time t (drift, bob, frame-by-frame flicker); the renderer paints each cell as a stitch.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 485 lines

**Uses:** [`core/art/draw.mjs`](../core/art/draw.mjs) · [`core/art/palette.mjs`](../core/art/palette.mjs) · [`core/art/sprites.mjs`](../core/art/sprites.mjs) · [`core/art/spec.mjs`](../core/art/spec.mjs)

**Used by:** [`pipeline/art.test.mjs`](../pipeline/art.test.mjs) · [`pipeline/features.test.mjs`](../pipeline/features.test.mjs) · [`web/js/art-view.mjs`](../web/js/art-view.mjs) · [`web/js/thumbs.mjs`](../web/js/thumbs.mjs)

**Exports:** `W`, `H`, `composeScene`, `describeScene`

### `core/art/concepts.mjs`

**What it is.** The dictionary that says which words in a verse mean which picture.

**How it is done.** Word lists with weights for about 70 figures (a lamb, a fish, a cross...), 12 settings, times of day (night, dawn, evening; day is the default), 6 moods with word lists (calm is the default), plus defaults for each of the 66 books. Weak hints end in `_soft`. God and Christ are never drawn as people: "God" and "Lord" only push a scene towards glory (light, heaven), and Christ-words towards the cross, lamb, shepherd or light. `lite()` trims plurals so "lambs" finds "lamb".

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 189 lines

**Used by:** [`core/art/spec.mjs`](../core/art/spec.mjs) · [`pipeline/art.test.mjs`](../pipeline/art.test.mjs)

**Exports:** `SPRITE_WORDS`, `SETTING_WORDS`, `TIME_WORDS`, `MOOD_WORDS`, `GLORY_WORDS`, `BOOK_DEFAULTS`, `lite`, `SPRITE_INDEX`, `SETTING_INDEX`, `TIME_INDEX`, `MOOD_INDEX`, `GLORY_SET`

### `core/art/draw.mjs`

**What it is.** A tiny pixel drawing kit: the `Grid`, shape primitives, the outline-and-shade finish, and the seeded random generator.

**How it is done.** A Grid holds palette indices (0 is transparent). Primitives: rectangle, ellipse, line, polygon (even-odd fill), stamp. `sprite()` draws a figure on a canvas with a 1-stitch margin, darkens the lower edge of each shape, then adds the dark outline, which gives every figure the same padded yarn look. `rng()` is the mulberry32 generator, so a verse always gets the same picture.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 142 lines

**Uses:** [`core/art/palette.mjs`](../core/art/palette.mjs)

**Used by:** [`core/art/compose.mjs`](../core/art/compose.mjs) · [`core/art/sprites.mjs`](../core/art/sprites.mjs) · [`pipeline/make-icons.mjs`](../pipeline/make-icons.mjs)

**Exports:** `Grid`, `sprite`, `rng`

### `core/art/palette.mjs`

**What it is.** The yarn palette (36 colours) and the colour grading for time of day and mood.

**How it is done.** Every pixel is an index into this list, so a scene can be re-coloured (dawn, evening, night, storm, fiery, holy) by changing the palette without changing any pixel. `SHADE` gives the darker yarn used for the lower edge of shapes.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 76 lines

**Used by:** [`core/art/compose.mjs`](../core/art/compose.mjs) · [`core/art/draw.mjs`](../core/art/draw.mjs) · [`pipeline/art.test.mjs`](../pipeline/art.test.mjs) · [`pipeline/make-icons.mjs`](../pipeline/make-icons.mjs)

**Exports:** `KEYS`, `HEX`, `C`, `PALETTE_SIZE`, `SHADE`, `RGB`, `grade`

### `core/art/spec.mjs`

**What it is.** Reads a verse and decides what its picture shows, and stores those decisions compactly.

**How it is done.** `makeSpec` counts picture words across four English versions (more versions give a steadier reading), picks one main figure and up to two more, the setting, the hour and the mood, and falls back to the book's defaults when a verse names nothing picturable. A spec is six numbers; `encodeSpecs`/`decodeArt` read and write `art.bin` (8 bytes of header, 4 bytes per verse reference, 6 bytes per verse: 304 KB for the whole Bible).

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 152 lines

**Uses:** [`core/english.mjs`](../core/english.mjs) · [`core/art/sprites.mjs`](../core/art/sprites.mjs) · [`core/art/concepts.mjs`](../core/art/concepts.mjs)

**Used by:** [`core/art/compose.mjs`](../core/art/compose.mjs) · [`pipeline/art.test.mjs`](../pipeline/art.test.mjs) · [`pipeline/build-art.mjs`](../pipeline/build-art.mjs) · [`pipeline/features.test.mjs`](../pipeline/features.test.mjs) · [`web/js/art-view.mjs`](../web/js/art-view.mjs) · [`web/js/data.mjs`](../web/js/data.mjs)

**Exports:** `SETTINGS`, `TIMES`, `MOODS`, `SPRITE_LIST`, `tokensOf`, `hashRef`, `makeSpec`, `encodeSpecs`, `decodeArt`

### `core/art/sprites.mjs`

**What it is.** The library of 75 crochet figures (animals, people, things, buildings) and their animation frames.

**How it is done.** Each figure is drawn from primitives by a small function rather than typed pixel by pixel; `sprite()` adds the outline and shading. Animated figures have two frames: a dove's wing up and down, a fish's tail flick, a grazing lamb, a serpent's tongue, flickering flames, lamps, candles and altars. `FPS` sets each one's frame rate.

**Runs in:** Browser + Node · 435 lines

**Uses:** [`core/art/draw.mjs`](../core/art/draw.mjs)

**Used by:** [`core/art/compose.mjs`](../core/art/compose.mjs) · [`core/art/spec.mjs`](../core/art/spec.mjs) · [`pipeline/art.test.mjs`](../pipeline/art.test.mjs) · [`pipeline/make-icons.mjs`](../pipeline/make-icons.mjs)

**Exports:** `person`, `house`, `SPRITES`, `ANIMATED`, `getSprite`, `getFrames`, `BIRD`, `FPS`, `SPRITE_NAMES`

## pipeline/: build tools and tests (Node only)

### `pipeline/art.test.mjs`

**What it is.** Tests for the pictures.

**How it is done.** Checks that every figure draws something and uses real colours, that every dictionary entry points at a real figure, that the scene writer reads verses sensibly (Psalm 23 gives a shepherd and lamb, Jonah a fish), that `art.bin` round-trips and covers every verse, that famous verses get fitting pictures, that scenes are fully covered and animate without error, that verses with the same subject still get different pictures (more than 97% distinct), and that the idle animation really moves.

**Runs in:** Node (build) · 129 lines · 9 tests

**Uses:** [`core/art/sprites.mjs`](../core/art/sprites.mjs) · [`core/art/palette.mjs`](../core/art/palette.mjs) · [`core/art/compose.mjs`](../core/art/compose.mjs) · [`core/art/spec.mjs`](../core/art/spec.mjs) · [`core/art/concepts.mjs`](../core/art/concepts.mjs) · [`pipeline/node-bible.mjs`](../pipeline/node-bible.mjs) · `node:test` (built into Node) · `node:assert/strict` (built into Node) · `node:fs` (built into Node) · `node:path` (built into Node) · `node:crypto` (built into Node)

**Used by:** npm test

### `pipeline/build-art.mjs`

**What it is.** Writes `dist/data/art.bin`: one scene description for every verse.

**How it is done.** Reads each verse in KJV, WEB, ASV and BSB from the built shards, runs `makeSpec` on them, encodes the result and adds the file to `manifest.json`. Prints how many verses got each setting, mood and main figure.

**Runs in:** Node (build) · 49 lines

**Uses:** [`pipeline/node-bible.mjs`](../pipeline/node-bible.mjs) · [`core/art/spec.mjs`](../core/art/spec.mjs) · `node:fs` (built into Node) · `node:zlib` (built into Node) · `node:path` (built into Node) · `node:url` (built into Node) · dist/data (built by build-data.mjs)

**Used by:** npm run build · npm run build:art

**Exports:** `buildArt`

### `pipeline/build-data.mjs`

**What it is.** Turns the downloaded Bible texts into the data files the app uses: `core.db`, one database per version, and `manifest.json`.

**How it is done.** Parses all texts first so the canonical verse list is the union over all versions. Each version becomes its own database with a `texts` table and a contentless FTS5 index (English: Porter stemming plus archaic folding; Tamil: the vowel-protected script index plus the sound index). English text has paragraph marks and brackets removed; Tamil text is stored exactly as published. `manifest.json` records sizes (plain and gzipped) and the build time, which the app uses to refresh its offline copies.

**Runs in:** Node (build) · 140 lines

**Uses:** [`core/books.mjs`](../core/books.mjs) · [`pipeline/versions.mjs`](../pipeline/versions.mjs) · [`core/tamil.mjs`](../core/tamil.mjs) · [`core/english.mjs`](../core/english.mjs) · [`pipeline/vpl.mjs`](../pipeline/vpl.mjs) · `node:sqlite` (built into Node) · `node:fs` (built into Node) · `node:zlib` (built into Node) · `node:url` (built into Node) · `node:path` (built into Node) · data/raw (downloaded texts) · node:sqlite · node:zlib

**Used by:** npm run build

**Exports:** `ROOT`, `DATA_DIR`, `build`

### `pipeline/docs.test.mjs`

**What it is.** Keeps the documentation honest.

## server/: local web server

### `server/server.mjs`

**What it is.** The small web server for working on the app locally (`npm run serve`, then open http://localhost:4321).

**How it is done.** Serves four folders under one address: the app (`web/`) at `/`, `core/` at `/core/`, the SQLite WebAssembly files at `/vendor/sqlite/`, and the built data at `/data/`. Refuses any path that leaves those folders, compresses text and database files with gzip (cached in memory), and answers revalidation with ETags. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only. The folder layout it presents is exactly the layout `npm run export` produces.

**Runs in:** Node (build) · 93 lines

**Uses:** `node:http` (built into Node) · `node:fs/promises` (built into Node) · `node:zlib` (built into Node) · `node:util` (built into Node) · `node:url` (built into Node) · `node:path` (built into Node)

**Used by:** [`pipeline/server.test.mjs`](../pipeline/server.test.mjs) · npm run serve · .claude/launch.json (the preview pane)

**Exports:** `MOUNTS`, `createServer`

### `web/js/crochet.mjs`

**What it is.** Draws a scene as crochet and plays the crocheting animation.

**How it is done.** Each cell is a stitch tile (a darker gap, two slanted legs, highlights) drawn once per colour and reused. The reveal works bottom row first, each row in the opposite direction like real crochet, with a hook that rocks as it works, yarn that sways in from the corner, a shimmer on freshly worked stitches, and a band of light sweeping across at the end. After that only the cells that change are repainted, ten times a second, for the idle animation. Speeds: slow 7 s, normal 3.8 s, fast 1.7 s.

**Runs in:** Browser · 259 lines

**Used by:** [`web/js/art-view.mjs`](../web/js/art-view.mjs)

**Exports:** `SPEEDS`, `CrochetCanvas`

### `web/js/data.mjs`

**What it is.** Loads the Bible data in the browser and opens it with SQLite.

**How it is done.** Starts SQLite WebAssembly, reads `manifest.json`, downloads `core.db` and `art.bin`, and downloads each version's database with progress, opening it from memory (`sqlite3_deserialize`). All addresses are built from the app's own folder, so it works under a sub-folder. Data URLs carry `?v=<build time>` so a new build is fetched while old offline copies are dropped. Versions can be unloaded (memory) or removed (offline copy).

### `web/sw.js`

**What it is.** The service worker that makes the app work offline.

**How it is done.** Downloaded Bible data (`data/*.db`, `art.bin`) is cache-first: fetched once, kept on the device. Everything else is network-first, so updates arrive when online and the cached copy is used when offline. It works out its own folder from its scope, so it behaves the same at a site root or in a sub-folder. Partial (range) responses are never cached.

**Runs in:** Browser · 50 lines

**Used by:** web/js/app.mjs registers it
